answer: Every epoch each identity must rotate its stake to a fresh address inside a narrow random window, like turning an onyx coin that cannot be split: the operator's ocean of fakes pays one on-chain fee per fake. With k fakes crowding one window, base fees rise super-linearly (EIP-1559 congestion), so the k-th fake costs more than the first. A dawn audit marks missed rotations ungradable; batching at the edge spikes the fees that erase the margin.
